title: Champions vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-07

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py (sha256 5c7b7aa4... identical across all domain verifiers and /root/ptocontri/pkg), latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue aclnn call(s) + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; aclnn executor fetched once via *GetWorkspaceSize, marked repeatable, reused across rounds (analogous to the pypto kernel being compiled once). Both sides are end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: m-tier decision preset {M:4096, N:4096}; dtype = champion's native contract dtype (bf16)

aclnn_baseline_semantics: aclnnGeluV2(approximate=tanh) — the tanh approximation matches the champion's formula exactly (y = 0.5x(1+tanh(sqrt(2/pi)(x+0.044715x^3)))). Single native op, no decomposition needed.

results.note: aclnnGeluV2 is ~1.23x faster at 4096x4096. Note the frozen-verifier holdout numbers (68.64 us) are geomeans over sealed shapes, not this preset point; the pypto number here is a fresh frozen-harness run at this exact shape.

convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
